summary: Reverified only s1_creativity_llm_vs_human_pooled and s2_creativity_constrained_vs_batch_pooled. Read the entire supplied markdown conversion through the references and end matter, extracted the cited PDF pages with PyMuPDF, and inspected in-memory rendered crops of the equations on PDF pp. 5-6. All six script flags are false positives caused by the PDF mathematical-font text encoding or flattened subscripts. On PDF p. 5, the objective expert-rated creativity paragraph prints Mhuman = 2.311, s.d. = 0.469; MLLM = 2.45, s.d. = 0.453; t202 = −2.154; P = 0.032; d = −0.301; 95% CI (−0.266, −0.012). These are objective scores despite the surrounding Self-reported creativity heading. The recorded negative signs preserve the printed human-minus-LLM orientation, as explained in the extraction. The interval estimand and d standardizer are not identified, so their uncertainty is appropriately retained. On PDF p. 6, the objective creativity ANOVA prints the LLM response-type main effect F1,200 = 0.811, P = 0.369, partial eta squared = 0.004; both degrees of freedom are visibly printed. The N = 204 captions on PDF p. 6 (Fig. 2) and p. 7 (Fig. 4) identify the analyzed samples for S1 and S2. Pooled arm counts are not printed in the supplied article and remain null. The outcome, arms, question, construct, measure, participant unit and uncertainty basis, higher_is, AI availability, immediate timing, between-participant coding, and comparison types are correct for both estimates. No additional eligible full-sample outcome/contrast is missing from the supplied ten-page article under extraction rules 4-6. Alternate S1 ANOVAs describe the same outcome and arm contrast; task-conditional creativity and fixation results are moderation results; self-reports are excluded. Completeness is limited to the supplied article: its separate supplementary material is not appended or embedded, no matching local supplement was found, and urllib requests to both the publisher article and the named OSF project API failed with WinError 10013. No supplement-only counts or outcomes were assumed absent.
